title: Rast wins Red Bull Ring Race 2 after Green's late gearbox trouble
dek: René Rast won Race 2 at the Red Bull Ring for Audi Sport Team Rosberg when pole-sitter Jamie Green lost his gearbox with laps to go, leaving Rockenfeller second and Müller third in a second Audi sweep.

chapters.title: Audi sweep Saturday
text: Saturday had belonged to Audi. Mattias Ekström won Race 1 from third on the grid, 0.398 seconds ahead of pole-sitter Jamie Green, with Nico Müller third, and the Swede left the first race on 162 points, 28 clear of Green and 31 clear of Lucas Auer, who had finished eighth at home. René Rast, a title contender before the weekend, was thirteenth and scored nothing, dropping to fifth on 124. With three races left, Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass said the team had not known where it would stand at equal weight, but that the RS 5 DTM had proved fastest.

chapters.title: Green on pole again, Ekström only eighth
text: Green took pole for the second day running, with a 1:21.955 that was 0.018 seconds quicker than his Saturday time. René Rast, who had put the other Rosberg car alongside him on 1:22.010, was 0.055 seconds behind, and Marco Wittmann was third on 1:22.156, again splitting the Audis. Rast said an error on his first lap in Saturday's qualifying had damaged his car and left his second run with little to give, whereas this time he had a clean run on both sets of tyres.

Mike Rockenfeller and Müller set identical 1:22.206s for fourth and fifth, and Gary Paffett's 1:22.243 made him the only Mercedes driver in the top ten, in sixth. Timo Glock was seventh. Ekström, the championship leader, managed only eighth on 1:22.337, ahead of Tom Blomqvist and Bruno Spengler. Edoardo Mortara, whose Mercedes had stopped in the morning practice session with a fuel-pressure problem, qualified fourteenth. Auer was slowest of the 18, on 1:22.682, just over seven tenths off the pole time.

chapters.title: Ekström pits at the end of lap one
text: Green kept the lead from Rast at the start. Ekström lost a place to Glock off the line and then made his mandatory stop at the end of the first lap, a gamble that Audi hoped would keep him out of the midfield battle and give him clear track to recover. Rockenfeller dropped behind Wittmann at the start but was soon challenging again.

After the stops Ekström came up behind Wittmann, who had stopped later and was working hard on his tyres, and could not get by. Wittmann managed to stay in front of him, and the BMW, Ekström and Rockenfeller ran in a tight group behind the two Rosberg cars.

chapters.title: Spengler spins Auer, and the field is bunched
text: In the second half of the race Bruno Spengler tried to outbrake Paul di Resta into the uphill hairpin at Turn 3 and hit Auer's Mercedes, spinning the home hero. The Mercedes struck the barrier, and Auer limped back to the pits with a damaged car, ending his race. The safety car was called, and Spengler was given a drive-through penalty for the contact.

Green and Rast had held a big lead over Müller, Wittmann, Rockenfeller and Ekström, and it was erased, with time for around eight more laps. The restart was made in double file, and Maro Engel was also given a drive-through for leaving the formation. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz said afterwards that a rival's approach had simply been too hard and that it had cost the team three cars.

chapters.title: Green's gearbox hands Rast the win
text: The restart reshuffled the middle of the field. Wittmann fell back as Rockenfeller and Ekström got past him, and for a while there were five Audis at the front before Paffett split them by taking fifth from Ekström. Ekström and Wittmann made contact as they fought on, and Ekström came out of the fight ahead to hold fifth.

Up front Green had led from the start, but with two or three laps left he reported that he could not change gear, slowed with smoke trailing from the car, and was swept past by the whole field before finishing fourteenth. Rast inherited the lead and won after 39 laps, a lap fewer than on Saturday, in 57:21.893. On the final lap Müller moved aside to let Rockenfeller take second, 1.025 seconds behind the winner, with Müller 1.824 seconds back in third. Paffett was fourth, 3.741 seconds behind, then Ekström, Wittmann and Glock, while Loïc Duval, who had started from the back of the grid and stopped late, finished eighth ahead of Paul di Resta and Wickens.

chapters.title: Audi double up, Wittmann cries foul
text: Rast's third win of the season came with mixed feelings. He said he would rather not have won this way, that Green had earned the victory and that the team had missed a Rosberg one-two. Green, who said he had been unable to shift gear three laps from the end, described his race as fine and the day as simply not his. Gass said Green had been the strongest driver of the weekend and that a small thing had cost him the win, but called the result, a second Audi podium sweep, fantastic for the brand. Müller said a second podium in a weekend felt good after a difficult year. Rockenfeller, who started fourth and finished second, called the restart his highlight and said he had held off Wittmann after it. Ekström, fifth after his lap-one stop, said he had surely had the worst tyres in the field at the restart and felt sorry for Green.

Wittmann was angry. He said Müller had held him up and let Ekström close in, that Rockenfeller and Ekström had pushed him out at the restart, and that Audi did not need to wreck other drivers' races when it was clearly faster. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt also criticised the tactical games. Audi's Abt team principal Thomas Biermaier rejected the criticism of Müller, saying he had done nothing wrong or unfair. At Mercedes, Fritz was upset that Auer had been taken out through no fault of his own, though he praised Paffett's performance in fourth.

The standings tightened at the top and thinned everywhere else. Ekström led on 172 points, with Rast second on 151, 21 behind, Green third on 137, and Rockenfeller and Wittmann level on 134. Auer, on 131, was 41 points adrift after his retirement, and with only a limited number of points left he was effectively out of the title fight. Wittmann was 38 off the lead and said a successful defence was theoretically possible but unlikely.

Six drivers, four of them in Audis, still had a chance of the title going into the finale at Hockenheim on 14 and 15 October. Ekström said he would again attack at full speed there, while Gass expected a hot finale and noted that the two Hockenheim races earlier in the season had been evenly matched.

facts.v: René Rast's win was his third of 2017 and moved him to second in the standings, 21 points behind Ekström.
